newsitem.title: ITALY: Monti says Italy budget worth recesssion risks.
newsitem.headline: Monti says Italy budget worth recesssion risks.

text.p: European Union Commissioner Mario Monti said on Saturday Italy's tough 1997 draft budget could have recessionary effects on the economy but that it was "worth the risk" given "what is at stake".

Monti, the EU's single market commissioner, said the centre-left government's budget bill, which aims to shave 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit, had given Italy a chance to join the first countries into a single European currency.
"With this budget, it is possible" to respect the timetable for economic and monetary union in 1999, Monti said in a speech at Milan's Bocconi University, of which he was once rector.
"Before, that would not have been possible," he added.
He said the budget, a mix of spending cuts and greater revenues, risked throwing Italy's economy into recession.
"But to me it seems that what is at stake at the moment is so important for Italy's place in the coming decades in the world economy that it would justify even a brief recession," Monti said.
